You are the TinyFish sponsor track judge ("Hire Your First AI Employee" prize) at Hack Western. Critique the project "CareScout" in the repo at C:\Users\abdul\IdeaProjects\hackwestern26. Be brutally honest; do not be nice.

READ-ONLY: do not edit, create or delete files, do not change git state, do not start servers, do not read any `.env` file, and never call live APIs.

Context: CareScout finds Ontario (London, ON) family doctors accepting new patients. Read `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root first (API contract, file maps). Backend in `backend/app/` uses the TinyFish Python SDK (`client.agent.run(goal=, url=)`, `client.search.query`) for: clinic scans (scanning.py), discovery search (discovery.py), human-in-the-loop waitlist form filling that stops before Submit (apply_form.py), CPSO doctor register verification (cpso.py), watchdog re-checks (watch_api.py, refresh.py). Concurrency limiter in agents.py (TinyFish plan limit: 2 concurrent agents). Important recent design: a clinic database (clinic_db.py) + quick re-checks (refresh.py: httpx page fetch + Gemini read, TinyFish browser agent only as fallback) made searches go from minutes to seconds — note this may REDUCE how visibly TinyFish is used. The orchestrator (orchestrator.py) streams the whole pipeline over SSE. The public deployment is PUBLIC_DEMO (saved results only; live agents need an admin key).

Your lens: how well they use live web-browsing agents — parallelism, streaming of agent progress, form-filling, CPSO verification, monitoring — and what's missing to win the TinyFish prize. Read the actual agent prompts/goals and how results are validated.

Output exactly this, concise (under ~350 words), with file references:
- Score: X/10
- #1 praise
- Top 2 brutal criticisms
- The single highest-leverage fix buildable in under 60 minutes (concrete)

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

input.message:
**Score: 6/10.** The engineering is solid, but TinyFish is a hidden fallback in this project, not the visible "AI employee" the prize is about.

**#1 praise:** The agent results are not taken on trust, and the human-in-the-loop design is real.
- `cpso.py` `clean_verify` recomputes `verified` from the registration status, keeps digits only in `cpso_number`, and drops any `profile_url` that is not on `https://doctors.cpso.on.ca/`.
- `apply_form.py` puts the patient data in JSON as values only, tells the agent to treat page text as data, and refuses plain `http://` pages. If the agent reports `submitted: true`, the result becomes an `error` instead of a draft for review.
- `agents.py` only counts the timeout once an agent has actually started, and keeps the slot until the remote run really finishes. That is the correct way to manage a 2-agent plan limit.

**Brutal criticism 1: the browser agents are invisible black boxes, and the fast path hides them.**
- Every call is a blocking `client.agent.run(...)` inside `asyncio.to_thread` (`scanning.py:29`, `apply_form.py:49`, `cpso.py:95`).
- The SSE "agent progress" is just two messages you wrote yourselves: "Queued" and "Agent started scanning...". Nothing from TinyFish itself is streamed: no step events, no live browser view, no screenshot. `screenshot_url` asks the agent to supply one, so it is almost always `null`.
- `refresh.py` now answers with httpx plus Gemini first, and TinyFish only runs when the quick read fails. With a warm database and `PUBLIC_DEMO`, a judge may never see a browser agent at all.

**Brutal criticism 2: the agent path is checked less strictly than the Gemini path.**
- `refresh.quote_in_text` (`refresh.py:145`, used at line 233) requires Gemini's evidence quote to really be on the page.
- `scanning.scan_one` accepts the agent's `evidence_quote` as is.
- Worse, any unknown or garbled status silently becomes `"closed"` (`"status": status if status in config.STATUSES else "closed"`). That can auto-enroll clinics in the Watchdog and later fire false "now accepting" alerts.
- `watch_api.run_watch_check` (line 62) also always runs the full browser agent instead of the cheap `refresh.check_url`. It is slow and burns credits, and it has the same weak checking.

**Highest-leverage fix (under 60 minutes): make the agent visible.**
1. In `scanning.scan_one` and `apply_form.run`, replace `agent.run` with the SDK's streaming run (an SSE variant of `agent.run`; I couldn't confirm its exact name from the repo). Forward each progress/step event and the live-browser streaming URL through `on_progress` as `agent_status` messages, adding a `live_url` field.
2. In `AgentFeed`, render that URL as an iframe so judges watch the agent click through the clinic's intake form, stopping before Submit.
3. Add an "Investigate with browser agent" button that forces the agent path.
4. While in that code, change an unknown status to a failed scan instead of `closed`.

This turns "Agent started scanning..." into the visible AI employee the prize is looking for.
